messages:
Incident Bot: PAGER: elevated client TLS failures + DNS resolution blips for api.redwood.ai originating from APAC Cloudflare POPs starting 2025-02-09T03:12Z. Paging @Nora (oncall).

Nora (oncall): Acknowledged. Symptoms: repeated TLS alert records, intermittent NXDOMAINs from our recursive resolvers to CF nameservers, and spikes in 502/524 in APAC.

Ethan (eng-sre): Seeing the same. Quick metrics: 6-minute window 03:12Z-03:18Z, ~7% 5xx across ap-south-1 and ap-northeast-1. Traces show initial connect then immediate TLS alert (handshake aborted) or no DNS answer.

Priya (infra): Running queries:
```
# system resolver to CF
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short
104.21.60.33
172.67.215.99
```
But from an APAC test probe we got: `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` intermittently.

Jules (cust-ops): CS ping 1: we've got several support tickets from APAC customers about request timeouts and auth failures (token exchange failed due to TLS). Holding a short customer note until we know impact.

Datadog Bot: Alert: "TLS.handshake.errors.apac" fired at 2025-02-09T03:14Z. Note: metrics ingestion delayed ~90s during surge.

Nora (oncall): Action list: 1) gather origin logs/pcaps 2) check whether we changed any CF config 3) consider emergency bypass to direct-origin if CF outage persists. Priya please pull origin logs for 03:10-03:20Z.

Priya (infra): Origin logs (sample):
```
2025-02-09T03:13:22Z cf-edge=104.21.60.33 "POST /v1/chat" 502 "upstream SSL handshake failed"
2025-02-09T03:13:28Z cf-edge=172.67.215.99 "GET /v1/health" 524 "upstream timeout during TLS handshake"
```
PCAP captured and uploaded to support ticket. No infra-config changes on our side in last 48h.

Ethan (eng-sre): Reproduction: from a Tokyo worker node: curl shows immediate TLS failure; from US node works fine.
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:104.21.60.33
* Connected to 104.21.60.33 (104.21.60.33) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3, TLS handshake, ClientHello (1)
* TLS alert received, handshake aborted
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failed: alert protocol version
```

Nora (oncall): Contacting Cloudflare NOC and opening ticket now. Also lowering DNS TTL to 30s for rapid switch if we need to. Jules prepare a short customer-facing blurb: "We're investigating degraded API connectivity for some APAC clients; engineers are working on mitigation."

Cloudflare Support Bot: New ticket 991122 opened: "Intermittent TLS handshake failures / DNS resolution issues in APAC POPs affecting multiple customers". NOC assigned. Please provide packet captures and origin timestamps.

Ethan (eng-sre): Two immediate mitigations to consider: A) switch api.redwood.ai to gray-cloud (bypass CF) for a short window; B) create a direct-failover hostname (direct-api.redwood.internal) and update DNS to point APAC CIDR ranges at it via GeoDNS. Pros/cons: A is fast but loses WAF and rate-limit; B is safer but takes longer to propagate.

Priya (infra): I can flip to gray-cloud for the api hostname quickly. We'll get direct traffic to origin but note the TLS cert is for api.redwood.ai, origin accepts it. We'll watch error rates and WAF logs.

Jules (cust-ops): If we bypass CF, we'll need to warn enterprise customers about temporary change and that some bot protections may be disabled. CS ready with templated note.

Nora (oncall): Proceeding with a cautious bypass: switching to gray-cloud now, TTL already low. Documenting rollback steps.

Priya (infra): Done 1: api.redwood.ai set to bypass Cloudflare proxy (DNS still at CF, but traffic goes direct).

Ethan (eng-sre): Monitoring: within ~60s from change, TLS handshake failures dropped from 7% -> 0.9% for APAC probes. Latency to origin increased slightly but errors are down.

Cloudflare Support Bot: Update on ticket 991122: NOC reports a partial regression in an edge TLS negotiation component affecting certain APAC POPs; engineers are rolling a hotfix. They recommend bypass until they confirm stability.

Datadog Bot: Secondary note: some alerts were suppressed due to ingestion lag; please cross-check raw logs for accurate counts.

Nora (oncall): Good. Keep bypass until CF NOC confirms fix. Action items captured: get full traces, update postmortem template, and review our emergency bypass runbook to include GeoDNS plan.

(approx 40 minutes pass)

Cloudflare Support Bot: Update: rollout hotfix completed in APAC POPs and TLS metrics are green. Recommend re-enabling proxy.

Priya (infra): Re-enabled Cloudflare proxy (orange-cloud) for api.redwood.ai. Re-checking metrics.

Ethan (eng-sre): Post-switch metrics: handshake success rate back to baseline, 5xxs < 0.3% and falling. No observed repeat of DNS NXDOMAIN incidents.

Jules (cust-ops): Sending final customer note: incident resolved; root cause: Cloudflare edge TLS regression in APAC; we briefly bypassed Cloudflare to restore connectivity. Following up with postmortem and customer impact details.

Nora (oncall): Handoff: Ethan will lead the postmortem. Key follow-ups:
- Consolidate timelines and affected customer list
- Add a GeoDNS failover option to runbook (steps + risk assessment)
- Confirm we keep TTL low for API hostlines during rollouts? Discuss in infra review.
- Ensure Datadog alert thresholds account for ingestion delays during surges

Ethan (eng-sre): Acknowledged. I'll pull logs, PCAPs, and Cloudflare ticket artifacts and draft the postmortem. Tagging owners for runbook updates. :thumbsup:

Nora (oncall): Closing paging. Thanks team.

Cloudflare Support Bot: Ticket 991122 resolved by NOC.

Ethan (eng-sre): Closing thread. Will post the postmortem draft in #postmortems when ready.
